title: Probing infrared eXcess to investigate early-Universe dust (PIXIEDust)
question: Examine the constraints on dust physics and obscured star formation in the z > 8 Universe by stacking deep (sub)mm observations of ten spectroscopically confirmed galaxies.

data.angular_resolution: 0.37 to 1.35 arcsec (stacked sample); down to 0.14 x 0.11 arcsec (MACS0416-Y1)
data.sensitivity: 3.0 to 65 uJy (individual observations); 2.0, 2.0, and 1.5 uJy 1-sigma depth in stacks at rest-frame 158, 88 um, and all data

what.value: NOEMA on-source time and continuum data for GN-z11

evidence.quote: For NOEMA data, the on-source time is taken from (cite: Fudamoto2024).

what.value: Published redshifts, M_UV, beta_UV, stellar masses, sizes, and lensing magnifications for the target galaxies

evidence.quote: Col. 7: The stellar mass estimate, corrected for lensing. The references can be found in the Appendix Section 6.

what.value: ALPINE sample (4.4 < z < 6) and REBELS / individual galaxy measurements (6 < z < 8) for comparison

evidence.quote: These are compared against lower redshift galaxies at $4.4 < z < 6$ from the ALPINE sample (cite: Sommovigo2022) and from REBELS and individual observations at $6 < z < 8$ (cite: Bakx2021; Sommovigo2022REBELS; Witstok2022; Fudamoto2022DustTemperatures; Algera2024; Algera2024REBELS25; Valentino2024).

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image individual ALMA continuum observations
recipe.method: Re-calibrate archival ALMA data using provided pipeline scripts and image continuum with TCLEAN onto a common pixel grid, extracting central source flux densities and noise.
assumptions: Sources are unresolved at the scale of the ALMA/NOEMA beams

recipe.method: Combine continuum images in the image plane using inverse-variance weighting at rest-frame 88 um, 158 um, across all data, and across bins of redshift, stellar mass, and beta_UV.
key_parameters: Bins: r.f. 88 um, r.f. 158 um, All, z > 9.5, z < 9.5, M_* > 10^9 M_sun, M_* < 10^9 M_sun, beta_UV > -2, beta_UV < -2
assumptions: Flux-based stacks are not corrected for gravitational lensing magnification

recipe.goal: Estimate infrared-based dust masses and perform dust-mass-weighted stacking
recipe.method: Convert individual continuum images from Jy/beam to M_dust/beam using a single-temperature optically-thin modified blackbody accounting for CMB heating, CMB contrast, and lensing magnification, then stack images with inverse-variance weighting; also compute conservative flux-based dust masses at average observing frequency and redshift.
key_parameters: T_dust(z=0) = 50 K, beta_dust = 2.0, kappa_0 = 10.41 cm^2 g^-1 at nu_0 = 1900 GHz
assumptions: Optically-thin dust emission; flat Lambda-CDM cosmology with Omega_m = 0.315, Omega_Lambda = 0.685, h = 0.674

recipe.method: Divide per-pixel dust mass images by published stellar masses to create dust-to-stellar mass ratio maps and stack them weighting by the standard deviation in dust-to-stellar mass ratio.
assumptions: Gravitational lensing affects stellar and dust components equally (no differential lensing)

recipe.goal: Estimate UV-based optical dust masses and compare with infrared limits and theoretical models
recipe.method: Compute optical dust masses from UV continuum slopes (beta_UV) and rest-frame UV/optical sizes using a foreground screen geometry and Meurer attenuation law, compute weighted averages across stacks, and compare against sub-mm limits and cosmological dust models.
key_parameters: f_mu = 4/3, tau_0 = 2.17 x 10^-8 (SMC), tau_1500 = 1.99 (beta_UV - beta_UV,intrinsic), beta_UV,intrinsic = -2.63, r_d = 100 pc (for REBELS-24 and GS-z9-3)
assumptions: Homogeneous dusty sphere foreground screen geometry; dust-emitting radius equals optical size of the source

score_reason: The authors release both the continuum FITS images and the complete Python/LINESTACKER analysis code on GitHub, and clearly state the equations, cosmology, dust parameters, and weighting schemes; only minor TCLEAN imaging parameters (exact cell size and line-masking channels for raw visibility re-imaging) are omitted from the text.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes are listed, the calibrated continuum images and stacking scripts are publicly released, and the main results are well-defined numeric upper limits on flux density, dust mass, and dust-to-stellar mass ratio.
